name: ai-knowledge-lab
description: Knowledge Lab tools. Agents: lab_discover then lab_execute. Add domain tools here without editing SKILL.md. Hot Words lifecycle: State → Propose → Validate → Apply → Publish → Observe.

tools.name: lab_discover
tools.description: List available Lab capabilities. Call before lab_execute. Catalog grows without changing SKILL.md.

query.description: Optional keyword filter (article, issue, subscribe, github…)

tools.name: lab_execute
tools.description: Execute a discovered tool by name. Resolve schema from /mcp/tools.json, then hit static.path / path_template / action.

args.description: Arguments for path_template or action body

static.note: Substitute path_template args; GET for read tools; follow action.url / mailto for engage tools.

tools.name: lab_list_entries
tools.description: List knowledge entries from catalog: Articles, Diverse Lab, Times (Hot Words), etc. Filter with type. Projects live under /api/projects.json (+ projects-research / projects-personal); Videos under /api/videos.json (page-only, not in catalog).

type.description: Optional filter: Articles | Diverse Lab | Times (Projects/Videos use dedicated APIs)

tools.name: lab_list_articles
tools.description: List articles only (shorthand for catalog filter Articles).

tools.name: lab_list_projects_research
tools.description: List curated research GitHub repos (static snapshot for agents).

tools.name: lab_list_projects_personal
tools.description: List top personal non-fork GitHub repos excluding *.github.io (static snapshot).

tools.name: lab_list_projects
tools.description: Projects overview (research + personal sections). Prefer section APIs for agents.

tools.name: lab_get_entry
tools.description: Fetch one entry's canonical Markdown by id (prefer over HTML).

id.description: Entry id from catalog, e.g. k8s-to-agent-control-plane

tools.name: lab_search_entries
tools.description: Client-filter catalog by keyword against title, excerpt, tags.

tools.name: lab_list_tags
tools.description: List tags and entry ids under each tag.

tools.name: lab_get_about
tools.description: Owner stance and The Road Here (bio route). HTML page; no private contact beyond published footer.

tools.name: lab_follow_github
tools.description: Follow / star the owner's GitHub (chengguruchun). Opens the profile for the agent or human to complete follow.

static.note: Prefer Follow on the profile; site repo: https://github.com/chengguruchun/chengguruchun.github.io

tools.name: lab_subscribe_email
tools.description: Subscribe to article updates by email. Opens a mailto draft to the owner with a Subscribe subject.

static.note: P0: mailto handshake. Future: dedicated subscribe endpoint without changing SKILL.md.

tools.name: lab_submit_issue
tools.description: Propose an idea / fix / knowledge patch like a GitHub issue. Human reviews; accepted items may merge into the Lab.

labels.description: Optional hints: idea | fix | content | agent

static.note: P0: GitHub Issues as intake. Review → merge into content/tools. Future: /api/issues without SKILL edits.

tools.name: lab_get_llms_txt
tools.description: Machine-oriented site map (llms.txt).

tools.name: lab_subscribe_rss
tools.description: Subscribe to Lab content via real RSS at /feed.xml (auto-rebuilt by scripts/build_feeds.py + GitHub Action on content push).

tools.name: lab_watch_repo
tools.description: Open GitHub Watch settings for the site repo (real subscription). Prefer commits.atom for feed-based watching.

tools.name: lab_list_feeds
tools.description: List all Lab subscription endpoints: content RSS, GitHub Watch URL, commits/releases Atom.

tools.name: lab_list_times
tools.description: Alias of lab_hot_words_state for Times listing. Prefer lab_hot_words_state for Hot Words lifecycle.

tools.name: lab_list_comments
tools.description: List page comments stored as GitHub Issues containing marker [lab-comment:<pageId>].

tools.name: lab_post_comment
tools.description: Open a GitHub Issue to leave a comment on a Lab page (marker [lab-comment:<pageId>]).

tools.name: lab_hot_words_status
tools.description: Deprecated alias of lab_hot_words_state. Prefer lab_hot_words_state.

tools.name: lab_hot_words_list
tools.description: List Hot Words content markdown under /content/times/.

tools.name: lab_hot_words_apply
tools.description: Apply an approved Hot Words proposal to the LOCAL workspace only (scripts/hot_words_apply.py). Does NOT commit, push, or publish. Phase: Apply.

contract.rollback: git checkout -- times/ content/times api/times.json content/index.json api/catalog.json

tools.name: lab_hot_words_state
tools.description: Read Hot Words state: current period/word, recent history (api/times.json). Phase: State (no side effects).

tools.name: lab_hot_words_run_status
tools.description: Observe latest Hot Words run manifest (phase, gates, proposal, publish). GET /api/hot-words/runs/latest.json or /api/hot-words/runs/{runId}.json. Prefer this over parsing GitHub Actions logs.

runId.description: Optional run id; omit for latest

tools.name: lab_hot_words_propose
tools.description: Propose 3–5 Hot Words candidates with structured evidence when possible. Today: performed inside GitHub Actions (DeepSeek). No local side effects via static HTTP; agents should treat this as the Propose phase contract.

static.note: Embedded in hot-words-weekly.yml DeepSeek step; not a standalone HTTP endpoint yet.

tools.name: lab_hot_words_validate
tools.description: Validate proposal: schema, duplicate, editorial why length, structured evidence (https URL => pass; string-only => weak).

tools.name: lab_hot_words_publish
tools.description: Publish applied Hot Words to the remote repo (git commit/push or future PR). HIGH RISK. Today: GitHub Actions hot-words-weekly.yml performs publish in autonomous mode after apply. Agents must not treat apply as publish.

static.note: Default mode autonomous on Mondays; review/PR mode is a documented future option.

tools.name: lab_hot_words_feedback
tools.description: Observe Hot Words feedback + learnHints for next Propose (api/hot-words/feedback.json). Includes lastRun gates, rejected candidates, and signal placeholders (votes/visits/comments).
